rows.title: Drafts only; a person presses Send
rows.statement: The job reads and writes drafts. Send, forward, reply, move and delete are refused by its transport before a byte leaves, whatever the token would allow.
rows.lead: gmail.compose can send. The transport refuses the call before it is emitted, and a mutant without that guard turns the suite red.
rows.residual: The Gmail token itself can send; the allowlist in this program is what stops it.

rows.title: Least privilege, residual risk declared
rows.statement: Each connector asks for the narrowest scope that does the work, and what the code adds on top is written down.
rows.residual: Graph Mail.ReadWrite can delete, both tokens can read any message by id, the Todoist token reaches every project, and the Scaleway policies cover the whole project. These limits live in code or in the project layout; no allowlist stops a stolen token.

matrix.granted: gmail.readonly + gmail.compose: read everything, manage drafts, send.
matrix.code: List the configured label only; read by id; create a draft in the thread. Send, trash, modify, delete refused.
matrix.residual: The token can send. Draft header X-Triage-Key travels if a person sends it.

matrix.granted: Mail.ReadWrite delegated, no Mail.Send: create, read, update, delete in every folder.
matrix.code: List the configured folder, Drafts and Sent Items; createReply with body and marker only. Move, PATCH, DELETE refused.
matrix.residual: The token can delete and edit any message.

matrix.code: One item_add per request, configured project only, no due date; uuid per task.
matrix.residual: Titles are model-written from the email and leave the Scaleway region.

matrix.code: One POST route; no tools; strict output schema; added figures, dates and names refused.
matrix.residual: Email text goes to the model; invented promises pass the checks.
